name: Hemoglobin
what: Protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen around the body.
whyLow: Can be associated with low iron, vitamin deficiencies, or blood loss.
whyHigh: Can be associated with dehydration, smoking, or living at high altitude.
questions: Could my hemoglobin level be related to my diet or iron levels?
Should I get an iron or B12 test?

name: RBC Count
what: Red blood cells carry oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body.
whyLow: Can be associated with anaemia, nutritional deficiency, or bone marrow issues.
whyHigh: Can be associated with dehydration, smoking, or lung disease.
questions: Do I need further tests to find the cause?
Is this related to my haemoglobin level?

name: PCV / Hematocrit
what: Percentage of your blood volume made up of red blood cells.
whyLow: Can be associated with anaemia, blood loss, or nutritional deficiencies.
whyHigh: Can be associated with dehydration, smoking, or lung conditions.
questions: Is my PCV consistent with my hemoglobin level?
Do I need further evaluation?

name: MCV
what: Average size of your red blood cells.
whyLow: Can be associated with iron deficiency or thalassemia trait.
whyHigh: Can be associated with B12 or folate deficiency, or liver disease.
questions: Does this indicate iron or vitamin deficiency?
Should I get an iron studies panel?

name: MCH
what: Average amount of hemoglobin in each red blood cell.
whyLow: Can be associated with iron deficiency.
whyHigh: Can be associated with B12 or folate deficiency.
questions: Is this consistent with the MCV result?
Should I get a nutritional panel?

name: MCHC
what: Average concentration of hemoglobin in each red blood cell.
whyLow: Can be associated with iron deficiency anaemia.
whyHigh: Can be seen in hereditary spherocytosis or severe dehydration.
questions: Does this point to a specific type of anaemia?

name: RDW
what: Measures variation in the size of your red blood cells.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with iron deficiency, B12/folate deficiency, or mixed anaemia.
questions: Does the high RDW suggest a nutritional deficiency?

name: WBC Count
what: White blood cells help your body fight infection.
whyLow: Can be associated with viral infections, some medicines, or bone marrow issues.
whyHigh: Can be associated with infection, inflammation, or stress.
questions: Could a recent infection explain this?
Do I need a repeat test?

name: Neutrophils
what: Most common type of white blood cell; first responders against bacterial infection.
whyLow: Can be associated with viral infections or certain medicines.
whyHigh: Can be associated with bacterial infection, inflammation, or stress.
questions: Is this related to an active infection?

name: Lymphocytes
what: White blood cells important for immune memory and fighting viruses.
whyLow: Can be associated with steroid use or certain infections.
whyHigh: Can be associated with viral infections or chronic inflammation.
questions: Could a viral illness explain this?

name: Monocytes
what: White blood cells that help clean up dead cells and fight germs.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant on its own.
whyHigh: Can be associated with chronic infections, autoimmune conditions, or recovery from illness.
questions: Should I be concerned about the monocyte level?

name: Eosinophils
what: White blood cells involved in allergic responses and fighting parasites.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with allergies, asthma, or parasitic infections.
questions: Could allergies or asthma explain this?
Should I get tested for parasites?

name: Basophils
what: Least common white blood cells, involved in allergic and inflammatory responses.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with allergic reactions or certain blood disorders.
questions: Is the basophil level something to monitor?

name: Platelet Count
what: Small blood cells that help your blood clot.
whyLow: Can be associated with infections, certain medicines, or low vitamin levels.
whyHigh: Can be associated with inflammation, iron deficiency, or infection.
questions: Should this be rechecked?
Do my medicines affect platelets?

name: MPV
what: Average size of your platelets; larger platelets are younger and more active.
whyLow: Can be associated with bone marrow issues.
whyHigh: Can be associated with platelet destruction or increased production.
questions: Does the MPV help explain my platelet count?

name: ESR
what: A general marker of inflammation in the body.
whyLow: Usually not a concern.
whyHigh: Can be associated with infection, autoimmune disease, or inflammation.
questions: What could be causing inflammation?
Do I need a CRP test as well?

name: Fasting Glucose
what: Sugar level in your blood after fasting.
whyLow: Can happen with long gaps between meals or certain medicines.
whyHigh: Can be associated with insulin resistance or diabetes risk.
questions: Do I need an HbA1c test to confirm this?
What lifestyle changes would help?

name: Post Prandial Glucose
what: Blood sugar level measured 2 hours after a meal.
whyLow: Can be associated with reactive hypoglycemia.
whyHigh: Can be associated with impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes risk.
questions: Does this confirm a diabetes risk along with my fasting glucose?

name: HbA1c
what: Average blood sugar level over the past 2 to 3 months.
whyLow: Can be seen with some blood conditions or recent blood loss.
whyHigh: Can be associated with prediabetes or diabetes risk.
questions: What does this mean for my diabetes risk?
How often should I repeat this test?

name: Total Cholesterol
what: Overall amount of cholesterol in your blood.
whyLow: Can be associated with diet, thyroid issues, or liver conditions.
whyHigh: Can be associated with diet, family history, or low activity.
questions: What is my overall heart risk with these numbers?
Should I change my diet or exercise first?

name: LDL Cholesterol
what: Often called 'bad' cholesterol because it can build up in blood vessels.
whyLow: Usually not a concern, but can be associated with diet or other conditions.
whyHigh: Can be associated with diet high in saturated fat, family history, or low activity.
questions: Is my LDL level a concern for my age?
Would diet changes be enough, or do I need further tests?

name: HDL Cholesterol
what: Often called 'good' cholesterol because it helps clear other cholesterol.
whyLow: Can be associated with low activity, smoking, or diet.
whyHigh: Usually not a concern.
questions: How can I raise my HDL naturally?

name: VLDL Cholesterol
what: A type of cholesterol that carries triglycerides in the blood.
whyLow: Usually not a concern.
whyHigh: Can be associated with high triglycerides, obesity, or metabolic syndrome.
questions: Is my VLDL related to my triglyceride level?

name: Triglycerides
what: A type of fat in your blood, influenced by diet and sugar intake.
whyLow: Usually not a concern.
whyHigh: Can be associated with sugary or fatty foods, alcohol, or blood sugar issues.
questions: Could my diet or alcohol intake explain this?

name: Total Bilirubin
what: Yellow pigment made when red blood cells break down; processed by the liver.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with liver disease, bile duct obstruction, or conditions like Gilbert's syndrome.
questions: Could this be Gilbert's syndrome?
Do I need a liver function panel?

name: Direct Bilirubin
what: Bilirubin that has been processed by the liver.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with liver disease or bile duct blockage.
questions: Does this indicate a liver or gallbladder issue?

name: Indirect Bilirubin
what: Bilirubin that has not yet been processed by the liver.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with increased red blood cell breakdown (hemolysis) or Gilbert's syndrome.
questions: Is this related to my other bilirubin results?

name: SGOT / AST
what: Enzyme found in the liver and heart; helps assess liver health.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with liver injury, alcohol use, medicines, or heart conditions.
questions: Could my medications be causing this?
Should I get a full liver panel?

name: SGPT / ALT
what: Enzyme mainly found in the liver; a key marker for liver damage.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with liver inflammation, fatty liver, or medicines.
questions: Do I have fatty liver disease?
Should I avoid certain medications or alcohol?

name: ALP
what: Enzyme found in the liver and bones; helps assess liver and bone health.
whyLow: Can be associated with malnutrition or certain rare conditions.
whyHigh: Can be associated with liver disease, bile duct obstruction, or bone disorders.
questions: Is this a liver or bone issue?
Do I need further imaging or tests?

name: GGT
what: Enzyme found in the liver; very sensitive to alcohol or bile duct problems.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with alcohol use, liver disease, or bile duct issues.
questions: Is this related to alcohol intake?
Should I reduce alcohol consumption?

name: Total Protein
what: Combined measure of albumin and globulin in the blood.
whyLow: Can be associated with liver disease, malnutrition, or kidney problems.
whyHigh: Can be associated with chronic infection, inflammation, or liver disease.
questions: Should I look at my albumin and globulin individually?

name: Albumin
what: Protein made by the liver; keeps fluid in your blood vessels and carries substances.
whyLow: Can be associated with liver disease, malnutrition, or kidney disease.
whyHigh: Can be associated with dehydration.
questions: Is my liver or kidney function a concern?

name: Globulin
what: Group of proteins in the blood including antibodies.
whyLow: Can be associated with liver disease or immune deficiency.
whyHigh: Can be associated with chronic infection, inflammation, or autoimmune disease.
questions: Should I get an immunoglobulin panel?

name: A/G Ratio
what: Ratio of albumin to globulin; helps evaluate liver and immune function.
whyLow: Can be associated with liver disease, kidney disease, or overproduction of globulin.
whyHigh: Usually not a concern.
questions: What does the A/G ratio tell us along with my other liver tests?

name: Urea / BUN
what: Waste product from protein digestion, filtered by the kidneys.
whyLow: Can be associated with low protein diet or liver disease.
whyHigh: Can be associated with dehydration, high protein diet, or kidney issues.
questions: Does this indicate a kidney problem?
Should I adjust my protein intake?

name: Creatinine
what: Waste product filtered by the kidneys, used to check kidney function.
whyLow: Can be associated with low muscle mass.
whyHigh: Can be associated with dehydration, heavy exercise, or reduced kidney function.
questions: Do I need a repeat or a kidney function panel?

name: Uric Acid
what: Waste product from breaking down purines found in certain foods.
whyLow: Can be associated with certain liver or kidney conditions.
whyHigh: Can be associated with gout, kidney stones, or high-purine diet.
questions: Am I at risk for gout?
Should I change my diet?

name: Calcium
what: Mineral essential for bones, muscles, nerves, and heart function.
whyLow: Can be associated with vitamin D deficiency, parathyroid issues, or malnutrition.
whyHigh: Can be associated with parathyroid issues, excess vitamin D, or certain cancers.
questions: Should I get my vitamin D and parathyroid levels checked?

name: Phosphorus
what: Mineral that works with calcium for strong bones and teeth.
whyLow: Can be associated with vitamin D deficiency, malnutrition, or antacid use.
whyHigh: Can be associated with kidney disease or excess vitamin D.
questions: Is my phosphorus related to my calcium or vitamin D levels?

name: Sodium
what: Electrolyte that helps control fluid balance, nerve function, and muscle contraction.
whyLow: Can be associated with excess water intake, certain medicines, or hormonal issues.
whyHigh: Can be associated with dehydration or excess salt intake.
questions: Could my fluid intake or medications explain this?

name: Potassium
what: Electrolyte vital for heart rhythm and muscle function.
whyLow: Can be associated with certain medicines (diuretics), vomiting, or diarrhea.
whyHigh: Can be associated with kidney disease, certain medicines, or hemolyzed blood sample.
questions: Could my medications be affecting my potassium?

name: Chloride
what: Electrolyte that helps maintain fluid balance and acid-base balance.
whyLow: Can be associated with prolonged vomiting or certain kidney conditions.
whyHigh: Can be associated with dehydration or kidney disease.
questions: Is my chloride level related to my sodium result?

name: Iron
what: Mineral essential for making hemoglobin and carrying oxygen in the blood.
whyLow: Can be associated with iron deficiency anaemia, poor diet, or blood loss.
whyHigh: Can be associated with iron overload, liver disease, or excessive supplements.
questions: Should I get a ferritin and TIBC test?

name: TIBC
what: Measures the blood's capacity to bind iron with transferrin protein.
whyLow: Can be associated with iron overload, liver disease, or malnutrition.
whyHigh: Can be associated with iron deficiency anaemia.
questions: Does this confirm iron deficiency along with my iron level?

name: Ferritin
what: Protein that stores iron in the body; reflects total iron reserves.
whyLow: Can be associated with iron deficiency, even before anaemia appears.
whyHigh: Can be associated with inflammation, infection, liver disease, or iron overload.
questions: Do I need iron supplements?
Could inflammation explain the high ferritin?

name: TSH
what: Hormone that tells your thyroid gland how much hormone to make.
whyLow: Can be associated with an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism).
whyHigh: Can be associated with an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism).
questions: Do I need T3 and T4 tests as well?

name: T3
what: Active thyroid hormone that regulates metabolism, energy, and body temperature.
whyLow: Can be associated with hypothyroidism or severe illness.
whyHigh: Can be associated with hyperthyroidism.
questions: Should I see an endocrinologist?

name: T4
what: Main thyroid hormone; gets converted to the active T3 form.
whyLow: Can be associated with hypothyroidism.
whyHigh: Can be associated with hyperthyroidism or excess thyroid medication.
questions: Does the T4 result match my TSH level?

name: Free T3
what: Unbound (active) form of the T3 thyroid hormone.
whyLow: Can be associated with hypothyroidism or non-thyroidal illness.
whyHigh: Can be associated with hyperthyroidism.
questions: How does this compare with my TSH?

name: Free T4
what: Unbound (active) form of the T4 thyroid hormone.
whyLow: Can be associated with hypothyroidism.
whyHigh: Can be associated with hyperthyroidism or over-medication.
questions: Should my thyroid medication dose be adjusted?

name: Vitamin D
what: Vitamin that supports bones, muscles, and immunity.
whyLow: Can be associated with low sun exposure, diet, or absorption issues.
whyHigh: Usually linked to high-dose supplements.
questions: Do I need a supplement, and what dose is right for me?
How long before I should retest?

name: Vitamin B12
what: Vitamin needed for nerves and for making red blood cells.
whyLow: Can be associated with diet (especially vegetarian), or absorption issues.
whyHigh: Usually linked to supplements.
questions: Should I take a B12 supplement?

name: Folate
what: B vitamin essential for cell growth and making DNA; important in pregnancy.
whyLow: Can be associated with poor diet, alcohol use, or malabsorption.
whyHigh: Usually linked to supplements.
questions: Should I take a folic acid supplement?

name: CRP
what: Protein that rises when there is inflammation or infection in the body.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with infection, autoimmune conditions, or cardiovascular risk.
questions: What could be causing the inflammation?
Do I need further evaluation?

name: HBsAg
what: Screening test for Hepatitis B virus infection.
whyLow: A negative/non-reactive result means no current Hepatitis B infection detected.
whyHigh: A positive/reactive result may indicate active or chronic Hepatitis B infection.
questions: Do I need Hepatitis B vaccination?
Should I get further hepatitis testing?

name: HIV
what: Screening test for Human Immunodeficiency Virus.
whyLow: A negative/non-reactive result means no HIV antibodies detected.
whyHigh: A reactive result needs confirmation with further tests.
questions: Should I get a confirmatory test?

name: Urine pH
what: Measures how acidic or alkaline your urine is.
whyLow: Can be associated with high-protein diet, dehydration, or metabolic acidosis.
whyHigh: Can be associated with urinary tract infections or vegetarian diet.
questions: Is my urine pH related to my diet?

name: Urine Specific Gravity
what: Measures how concentrated your urine is.
whyLow: Can be associated with excess water intake or diabetes insipidus.
whyHigh: Can be associated with dehydration or heart failure.
questions: Am I drinking enough water?

name: Magnesium
what: Mineral important for muscle, nerve, and heart function.
whyLow: Can be associated with poor diet, alcohol use, or certain medicines.
whyHigh: Can be associated with kidney disease or excess supplementation.
questions: Should I take a magnesium supplement?

name: LDH
what: Enzyme found in many tissues; released when cells are damaged.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with tissue damage, haemolysis, liver disease, or certain cancers.
questions: What could be causing the elevated LDH?

name: CPK / CK
what: Enzyme found in muscles and heart; rises with muscle damage.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with intense exercise, muscle injury, or heart conditions.
questions: Could heavy exercise explain this?
Do I need a heart-specific CK-MB test?

name: Amylase
what: Enzyme that helps digest carbohydrates; mainly from the pancreas and salivary glands.
whyLow: Can be associated with chronic pancreatitis or cystic fibrosis.
whyHigh: Can be associated with acute pancreatitis, salivary gland issues, or kidney disease.
questions: Do I need a lipase test as well?

name: Lipase
what: Enzyme that helps digest fats; mainly from the pancreas.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with pancreatitis, gallstones, or kidney disease.
questions: Should I get pancreas imaging?

name: Reticulocyte Count
what: Young red blood cells just released from the bone marrow.
whyLow: Can be associated with bone marrow suppression or aplastic anaemia.
whyHigh: Can be associated with active blood loss, haemolysis, or recovery from anaemia.
questions: Does this help explain my anaemia?

name: Prothrombin Time
what: Measures how long it takes your blood to clot; used to monitor blood thinners.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with liver disease, vitamin K deficiency, or blood thinner therapy.
questions: Does my medication need dose adjustment?

name: INR
what: Standardised measure of blood clotting time; used to monitor warfarin therapy.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with liver disease or blood thinner therapy; target is often 2–3 on warfarin.
questions: Is my warfarin dose correct?

name: aPTT
what: Another clotting time test; assesses the intrinsic clotting pathway.
whyLow: Usually not clinically significant.
whyHigh: Can be associated with clotting factor deficiency or heparin therapy.
questions: Is a bleeding disorder possible?

name: GFR / eGFR
what: Estimates how well your kidneys filter waste from the blood.
whyLow: Can be associated with reduced kidney function (chronic kidney disease).
whyHigh: Usually not a concern.
questions: What stage of kidney function is this?
Do I need to see a nephrologist?

name: Bicarbonate
what: Helps maintain the acid-base balance of the blood.
whyLow: Can be associated with metabolic acidosis, kidney disease, or diarrhea.
whyHigh: Can be associated with vomiting, dehydration, or certain lung conditions.
questions: Is my acid-base balance a concern?
